facts.text: Golden Harvest had director Robert Clouse shoot China O'Brien II right after the first film, before the original had even been released.
Director Robert Clouse made Bruce Lee's Enter the Dragon (1973), then completed Lee's unfinished Game of Death with a new storyline and cast in 1978.
Star Cynthia Rothrock (Sheriff China O'Brien) was an undefeated World Karate Champion in forms and weapons for five straight years, 1981 to 1985.
Melanie Good, the birthday stripper in this scene, made her screen debut in China O'Brien II.
The mayor praises two crime-free years because the sequel is set two years after the first film, with China now sheriff and Matt and Dakota her deputies, per Den of Geek.
China dedicates her plaque to her late father, a cop. Film scholar Rikke Schubart says producers gave Cynthia Rothrock's character a slain-cop dad to make her seem more feminine and less threatening.
Cynthia Rothrock tore the ligament in her right knee in the mid-80s and skipped surgery. Doctors found her thigh muscles were strong enough to hold the kneecap in place without it.
Cindy Clark plays dispatcher Lucille. Den of Geek calls her a sassy desk sergeant and notes China's department now has women on staff, unlike in the first film.
Chester, the mountain man who gets drunk and wrecks Lizard's place, is one of the quirky small-town background characters Den of Geek singles out as a highlight of the sequel.
Richard Norton (Deputy Matt Conroy) worked as a bodyguard for Rod Stewart, David Bowie and Fleetwood Mac before becoming a screen fighter.
Before she was famous, Tori Amos recorded the song 'Distant Storm' for the first China O'Brien film under the fake band name Tess Makes Good.
Cynthia Rothrock is said to be the inspiration for Sonya Blade, the fighter in the Mortal Kombat video games.
Producer Fred Weintraub owned the Greenwich Village club the Bitter End, where he booked Peter, Paul and Mary and Lenny Bruce, and later oversaw Woodstock as a Warner Bros. executive.
Keith Cooke (Deputy Dakota) auditioned for Liu Kang in 1995's Mortal Kombat but was cast as the green ninja Reptile instead.
Variety called the first China O'Brien 'an okay showcase' for Cynthia Rothrock. Golden Harvest made both films to build her profile in America after her Hong Kong stardom.
Keith Cooke was born Keith Hirabayashi. Producer Fred Weintraub suggested the stage name Cooke, his mother's surname, as it sounded more all-American.
Richard Norton trained gymnast Kurt Thomas for Gymkata (1985) and helped choreograph it. Gymkata was directed by Robert Clouse, who also made this film.
Director Robert Clouse's Enter the Dragon cost about $850,000 and grossed an estimated $90 million worldwide. It was added to the U.S. National Film Registry in 2004.
Some fights were shot after principal photography to pad the running time. Billy Blanks was cast at short notice for a fight with Keith Cooke (Dakota).
Keith Cooke and Billy Blanks fought again in The King of the Kickboxers (1990). There Cooke's character dies off-screen at the hands of Blanks' villain, Khan.
Sandra Weintraub wrote the story for the first China O'Brien, and Den of Geek says a different writing team adapted her outline for this sequel. Her father Fred Weintraub produced both films.
Flickering Myth's review says Keith Cooke gets more to do here than in the first film. It also says Billy Blanks adds some edge as one of the drug-dealing thugs.
Richard Norton and Cynthia Rothrock co-starred in five martial arts films: both China O'Brien films, Lady Dragon, Rage and Honor, and Rage and Honor II.
Den of Geek's look back at the series points to the sequel's quirky fighters: a metal-clawed brawler, chefs who chop in unison and a whip-cracking Indiana Jones type.
Wikipedia notes fans rate the sequel level with the first film, though the film was criticised for another aging villain who can't fight and has no final showdown.
Golden Harvest stopped at two China O'Brien films. Den of Geek's retrospective laments that a TV series or books never followed, despite how well the sequel's action held up.
Cynthia Rothrock made her acting debut in Hong Kong's Yes, Madam (1985) opposite Michelle Yeoh, before Golden Harvest brought her to Hollywood-style roles like this one.
Richard Norton's first screen role was in Chuck Norris' The Octagon (1980). Fighting Stars magazine later ranked their fight #13 among the 25 greatest fight scenes ever.
Both China O'Brien films came out together on a double VHS in 1991, becoming rental-store staples for martial arts fans.
The film gets a nod in the documentary In Search of the Last Action Heroes (2019), which also features Cynthia Rothrock.
Richard Norton (Deputy Matt Conroy) died on March 30, 2025. He worked on more than 80 films and TV shows as an actor, stunt performer and fight choreographer.
